review_notes: Inspected all 107 lines of the target and downstream uses of the contraction lemmas in CalabiBochner and CalabiRicciContraction. The main formulas involving derivatives and connection symmetry have no clear canonical simp orientation; the contraction-at-identity theorem has a concrete downstream rewrite use. The proposed simp attribute should be checked against the project’s simp behavior before merging.

findings.excerpt:
lemma curvature_contraction_at_one {z : V n} (hz : z ∈ K.domain)
    (hM : K.matrix z = 1) : ∑ k, K.curvature k k z = K.ricciHessian z := by
findings.problem: This theorem gives a natural simplification when the metric matrix at the point is the identity, but it is not tagged `[simp]`. A downstream proof explicitly invokes `rw [K.curvature_contraction_at_one hz hM]` for the exact left-hand expression, so users must manually select a rewrite that could be applied automatically when the identity-matrix hypothesis is available.
findings.proposed_change: Consider tagging `curvature_contraction_at_one` with `[simp]`, keeping its current left-to-right orientation. The rule is conditional on `K.matrix z = 1` and rewrites a contracted curvature sum to `K.ricciHessian z`; it does not expand the right-hand side back into curvature.
findings.benefit: With `hM` in the local context, simplification can put the identity-frame contraction into the Ricci-Hessian normal form without a manual rewrite. The conditional rule also leaves non-identity points, including cases without the hypothesis, unchanged.
